title: 2008 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 10
statement: Let \(a, b, c\) denote the side lengths of \(B C, C A, A B\). Find the lengths of \(A E, B F, C D\) in terms of \(a, b, c\).

solutions.text:
Let \(x=A E=A F, y=B D=B F, z=C D=C E\). Since \(B C=B D+C D\), we have \(a=x+y\). Similarly with the other sides, we arrive at the following system of equations:

\[a=y+z, \quad b=x+z, \quad c=x+y .\]

Solving this system gives us

\[\begin{aligned}
& A E=x=\frac{b+c-a}{2}, \\
& B F=y=\frac{a+c-b}{2}, \\
& C D=z=\frac{a+b-c}{2}
\end{aligned}\]
